results.content: # Neng Wang. #### Chong Khoon Lin Professor of Real Estate and Finance at Columbia University. Neng Wang is Chong Khoon Lin Professor of Real Estate and Finance at Columbia Business School. He is also a Research Associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER). His research interests include corporate finance, risk management, private equity, hedge funds, entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial finance, asset allocation, investor protection, household finance, wealth and income distribution, macroeconomics, real estate finance, and the Chinese economy. ## Publications. ### DP15341 A q Theory of Internal Capital Markets. ### DP13202 Rare Disasters, Financial Development, and Sovereign Debt. ### DP4955 Agency Conflicts, Investment and Asset Pricing. ## Latest contributions. ### Tokenomics: Cryptocurrency valuation and the roles of tokens.

results.content: Add Paper to My Library. Using these links will ensure access to this page indefinitely. # Creditor-on-Creditor Violence. 193 Pages Posted: 9 May 2024 Last revised: 8 Dec 2025. See all articles by Samuel Antill. ## Samuel Antill. Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Finance; Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business. Distressed firms often raise liquidity by stripping collateral from syndicated-loan creditors and pledging it to new lenders---an emerging practice known as “creditor-on-creditor violence.” We model this phenomenon. This inefficiency resembles debt overhang: equity holders negotiate selfishly, potentially blocking surplus-enhancing financing, to reduce wealth transfers to existing creditors. By diverting collateral from existing creditors, equity holders capture more surplus from financing, aligning incentives and improving efficiency. Our theory explains why new debt contracts still permit creditor-on-creditor violence. **Keywords:** Continuous-time capital structure models, Liability management, Bankruptcy, Creditor-on-creditor violence, Dropdowns, Uptiers.
